Subject: Post-demo: semantic index migration & embedding spec — integration items

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Good discussion — the team had a few requests we promised to capture and a clear set of next steps so you can evaluate migration effort and cost. Quick recap and asks below.

Recap (from our end)
- Goal: Replace current vendor embeddings and move to Redwood-hosted embeddings + reranker for product search and similarity features. Preserve existing document IDs and minimize indexing downtime.
- Primary concerns you raised: model dimension compatibility, throughput for backfill, retrieval quality delta, and auth/ops requirements for production.

Specific technical items we discussed / need answers on
1) Current embedding config: which model & dimension are you using now (you mentioned ~384 dims).
2) Target vector dimension and storage: are you OK with moving to 1536 dims (higher quality) or prefer staying closer to current dims for storage cost reasons?
3) Batching/ingest window: expected documents for full backfill and max sustained ingestion throughput (docs/sec).
4) Similarity metric: do you currently index normalized vectors (cosine) or raw vectors (dot product)?
5) DB compatibility: confirm your vector DB (you mentioned Pinecone) and whether you can accept a brief export/import step.
6) Auth & network: will you require API key rotation via KMS, or need VPC/private deployment for traffic?

Proposed next actions from Redwood
- Rafael will draft a short ingestion plan (batch sizes, estimated GPU hours, estimated tokens / cost) and a migration playbook for a 2-phase rollout (pilot -> full backfill -> cutover).
- Rafael will include an opinion on dimension choice (1536 vs 768 vs keeping 384) with example precision@10 / cost tradeoffs (we attach benchmarks).
- Neha will follow up on pricing for reserved capacity/backfill credits and any discounting for migration work.
- Schedule: 30-min tech sync to run through ingestion playbook and DB compatibility next Tue/Wed.

Attachments: acme-migration-outline.pdf (migration checklist), embedding-benchmarks.csv (sample precision/cost table)

Can you confirm the answers for items 1–5 above and propose a 30-min slot for the tech sync?

Thanks —

Subject: RE: Post-demo: semantic index migration & embedding spec — integration items

Hi Sam / Priya —

Following up with a technical plan sketch so you have concrete recommendations to evaluate. I tried to keep it implementation-first.

High-level recommendation (two options)
- Quality-first: re-embed to 1536 dims (Redwood's recommended default for dense semantic search on retail catalogs). Expect ~6–12% P@10 improvement vs 384 dims in our benchmark for catalog-like queries; storage ~4x compared to 384.
- Cost-constrained: re-embed to 768 dims as a middle ground — most of the P@10 gains return by 768 with ~2x storage vs 384.

Similarity & normalization
- If your vector store supports cosine natively (pre-normalized), we recommend storing L2-normalized vectors to allow dot-product at query time and faster ANN configs.
- Alternatively, store raw vectors and keep a per-vector norm column if you want to run cosine on-the-fly (adds storage but gives flexibility).

Migration approach (2-phase)
1) Pilot: pick a 10k doc slice, re-embed, run A/B queries (current vs Redwood) to measure delta (P@10, MRR). Smoke test reranker on small set.
2) Full backfill: parallel ingest pipeline — 512 doc batches per worker, concurrent workers ramp to meet throughput. For GPU-accelerated bulk encode use batch size 512 and accumulate until ~8–12k tokens per GPU batch. We recommend checkpointing progress by original doc ID and embedding model version (embed_v=redwood-1536-2027-04) to support rollback.
3) Cutover: run both indices in parallel for X days (traffic slicing) then flip primary if metrics stable.

Routing / availability
- Primary inference region: us-west; failover us-east. We can provide a routing policy that pins production calls to us-west and falls back to us-east if latency or capacity thresholds are hit.

Auth & ops
- Standard hosted auth: API key + key rotation via our Admin console (we can also accept customer-provided KMS for key wrapping).
- If you need on-prem/VPC: Redwood Private supports mutual TLS + customer-managed KMS for signing short-lived tokens.

Reranker pattern
- 2-stage flow: (1) ANN retrieval using embeddings (recall-focused), (2) lightweight transformer reranker (rescore top N, typically N=50) that uses structured metadata and tool-calling outputs for context. This reduces overall API cost while improving precision.

Estimated sizing notes (back-of-envelope)
- Pilot (10k docs): ~2–3 GPU-hours.
- Full catalog (1.2M docs): ~120–200 GPU-hours depending on batch efficiency and whether you run mixed-precision kernels.
- Ingestion throughput target we can support: sustained ~10k docs/min with an autoscaled dedicated pool; bursts higher.

Compatibility with Pinecone
- We can export embeddings as CSV/NDJSON with doc_id, vector, model_version, norm. Pinecone import requires JSONL or their SDK; we can provide export helpers that generate Pinecone-ready JSONL.

Smoke tests / quality checks
- Precision@10, MRR, recall@100 for baseline queries (we'll reuse your query corpus). Also semantic drift checks on reranker outputs — we keep eval dashboards for regressions.

I'll turn this into a one-pager and attach it to the HubSpot deal. If you confirm current dims and total docs, I can produce a tighter GPU-hour & cost estimate.

— Rafael

Thanks Rafael — this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications so we can scope with our infra team:

1) Our current setup: Pinecone with 384-dim embeddings (legacy vendor). Total doc count ~1.15M (catalog + descriptions).
2) Storage constraints: we have a hard cap on index storage for cost reasons; leaning towards 768 dims if we can get 90% of the quality uplift.
3) Can you confirm the export helper you mentioned will produce Pinecone JSONL including norm and metadata?
4) For the reranker: we run the model inline today as a Lambda — what's the typical latency for the lightweight reranker on top-50 with 2–4 small transformer layers?

Also — are you able to provide any estimate for incremental monthly compute cost if we keep a hybrid: Pinecone for hot index + Redwood for embeddings and rerank on query path? We're trying to model op-ex vs cap-ex.

Happy to take the 30-min tech sync next Wed 10am PT if that works for your infra folks.

Thanks,
Sam Weston
